articles.author: Shashi Bhushan Kumar
articles.description:
Should a single user be able to react multiple times on the same post? 🤔


Recently I noticed something interesting while using a developer community platform.
A single user can react with multiple reaction types on the same post.
For example:
❤️ Like
One user can click several of these reactions on the same post.
On one hand, this is nice because it allows people to express different emotions about the same content.
But it also made me think about something from a user experience perspective.
If one person adds multiple reactions, the reaction count increases multiple times — even though it came from the same user.
For someone viewing the post, it might look like many people reacted, while in reality it could be just one person using several reactions.
So I’m curious to hear the community’s perspective.
• Allow multiple reactions from the same user
only one reaction per user
total reactions and number of unique users
I’d really like to hear what other developers think about this.
Do you think this behavior is good for engagement, or could it create confusion in reaction counts?
I also opened a discussion in the open-source repository behind this platform to understand the community perspective:
👉 https://github.com/forem/forem/discussions/22941
Would love to hear your thoughts 👇


Give Valuable Feedback In comment.👇
articles.title: Should One User Be Able to Add Multiple Reactions on the Same Post? 🤔

articles.author: Phantasm0009
articles.description:
Every data person has the same nightmare.
German client sends a CSV with semicolons, DD.MM.YYYY dates, and European number formatting. French client sends commas with DD/MM/YYYY. US client sends MM/DD/YYYY. You open each one with pandas.read_csv() and it silently corrupts all three.
I spent two years writing the same "detect encoding, guess delimiter, figure out date format" code for every new client. Last month I finally snapped and built a library.
Here's a typical European export file:
Kunden-Nr;Name;Datum;Umsatz;Aktiv
00742;Müller GmbH;01.03.2025;1.234,56;Ja
00123;Schäfer AG;15.07.2024;789,00;Nein
00456;Böhm & Co;25.12.2024;12.345,67;Ja

Semicolons as delimiters. Dots in dates. Commas as decimal separators. Leading zeros in IDs. Ja/Nein instead of True/False.
Watch what pandas does to …
